title: Rama meets Lakshmana
introduction: Rama meets Lakshmana while returning to hermitage after killing the deer demon Maareecha. He also confronts some ill omens and worries why Lakshmana left Seetha alone and came to him, sad facedly.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे सप्त पंचाशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 57th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
राक्षसम् मृग रूपेण चरन्तम् काम रूपिणम् |
निहत्य रामो मारीचम् तूर्णम् पथि न्यवर्तत
verses.iast:
rākṣasam mṛga rūpeṇa carantam kāma rūpiṇam |
nihatya rāmo mārīcam tūrṇam pathi nyavartata
verses.translation: Rama on killing that demon Maareecha, who is a guise changer at his wish and who moved about in the guise of a deer, instantly started to return on the trail by which he trailed after that deer-demon.

glosses.meaning: in deer's, guise, one who is moving about
quickly, on trail, started to return.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य संत्वरमाणस्य द्रष्टु कामस्य मैथिलीम् |
क्रूर स्वरो अथ गोमायुः विननाद अस्य पृष्ठतः
verses.iast:
tasya santvaramāṇasya draṣṭu kāmasya maithilīm |
krūra svaro atha gomāyuḥ vinanāda asya pṛṣṭhataḥ
verses.translation: While Rama is anxiously hurrying to see Maithili, then a brutish voiced jackal deafeningly howled at his behind.

verses.devanagari:
स तस्य स्वरम् आज्ञाय दारुणम् रोम हर्षणम् |
चिंतयामास गोमायोः स्वरेण परिशन्कितः
verses.iast:
sa tasya svaram āGYāya dāruṇam roma harṣaṇam |
ciṃtayāmāsa gomāyoḥ svareṇa pariśankitaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing that threatening and hair-raising howl of jackal Rama is overly threatened just by the tone of fox in which it is foreboding, inasmuch as the forbidding intoning of Maareecha.

glosses.meaning: of fox's, by tone, overly, doubtful [threatened]

verses.devanagari:
अशुभम् बत मन्ये अहम् गोमायुः वाश्यते यथा |
स्वस्ति स्यात् अपि वैदेह्या राक्षसैः भक्षणम् विना
verses.iast:
aśubham bata manye aham gomāyuḥ vāśyate yathā |
svasti syāt api vaidehyā rākṣasaiḥ bhakṣaṇam vinā
verses.translation: "Huh! As to how this jackal has howled I deem that as inauspicious. As yet undevoured by demons would Vaidehi be safe?

glosses.meaning: jackal, as to how, voicing - howling
safe, will be, albeit - is she safe?

verses.devanagari:
मारीचेन तु विज्ञाय स्वरम् आलक्ष्य मामकम् |
विक्रुष्टम् मृग रूपेण लक्ष्मणः शृणुयात् यदि
स सौमित्रिः स्वरम् श्रुत्वा ताम् च हित्वा अथ मैथिलीम् |
तया एव प्रहितः क्षिप्रम् मत् सकाशम् इह एष्यति
verses.iast:
mārīcena tu viGYāya svaram ālakṣya māmakam |
vikruṣṭam mṛga rūpeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ śṛṇuyāt yadi
sa saumitriḥ svaram śrutvā tām ca hitvā atha maithilīm |
tayā eva prahitaḥ kṣipram mat sakāśam iha eṣyati
verses.translation: "On knowing the nature of my voice Maareecha in the semblance of a deer yelled out mimicking my voice. If Lakshmana listens that voice, recognising it as my voice he will instantly rush to my near. Else if Maithili listens, she will hasten him to go over here and Soumitri instantly rushes here leaving her off.

glosses.meaning: on knowing - the nature of my voice
he, that Soumitri, [my] voice, on hearing [on recognising]
by her [by Seetha,] only, to here, hastened up
instantly, to my, near, he rushes.

verses.devanagari:
राक्षसैः सहितैर् नूनम् सीताया ईप्सितो वधः |
कांचनः च मृगो भूत्वा व्यपनीय आश्रमात् तु माम्
दूरम् नीत्वा अथ मारीचो राक्षसो अभूत् शर आहतः |
हा लक्ष्मण हतो अस्मि इति यत् वाक्यम् व्यजहार ह
verses.iast:
rākṣasaiḥ sahitair nūnam sītāyā īpsito vadhaḥ |
kāṃcanaḥ ca mṛgo bhūtvā vyapanīya āśramāt tu mām
dūram nītvā atha mārīco rākṣaso abhūt śara āhataḥ |
hā lakṣmaṇa hato asmi iti yat vākyam vyajahāra ha
verses.translation: "As could be seen from Maareecha's becoming a Golden Deer only to sidetrack and take me away from hermitage, his becoming a demon when hit with an arrow, and his shouting words indeed like, 'ha, Lakshmana, ha, Seetha, I am killed,' the demons are collectively intending to do away with Seetha. It is certain.

glosses.meaning: demon, as to how he became
sentence, as to how he uttered - shouted, indeed

verses.devanagari:
अपि स्वस्ति भवेत् द्वाभ्याम् रहिताभ्याम् मया वने |
जनस्थान निमित्तम् हि कृत वैरो अस्मि राक्षसैः
निमित्तानि च घोराणि दृश्यन्ते अद्य बहूनि च |
verses.iast:
api svasti bhavet dvābhyām rahitābhyām mayā vane |
janasthāna nimittam hi kṛta vairo asmi rākṣasaiḥ
nimittāni ca ghorāṇi dṛśyante adya bahūni ca |
verses.translation: "Whether there will be safety in forest for those two in my absence, or not, is my doubt. Owing to my devastating Janasthaana I have become a harboured grudge for demons, am not I! As such, foretokens are appearing now, severely and severally." Thus Rama's thoughts have sprinted.

glosses.meaning: by demons, made [harbours,] grudge [against me,] I am, am not I

verses.devanagari:
इति एवम् चिंतयन् रामः श्रुत्वा गोमायु निःस्वनम्
निवर्तमानः त्वरितो जगाम आश्रमम् आत्मवान् |
आत्मनः च अपनयनम् मृग रूपेण रक्षसा
verses.iast:
iti evam ciṃtayan rāmaḥ śrutvā gomāyu niḥsvanam
nivartamānaḥ tvarito jagāma āśramam ātmavān |
ātmanaḥ ca apanayanam mṛga rūpeṇa rakṣasā
verses.translation: When that soulful Rama has heard the whistle of jackal while returning, he persistently thought in this way about his detour caused by demon in the disguise of a deer, thus he speedily advanced towards his hermitage.

glosses.meaning: thus, in that way, persistently thought

verses.devanagari:
आजगाम जनस्थानम् राघवः परिशन्कितः |
तम् दीन मानसम् दीनम् आसेदुः मृग पक्षिणः
verses.iast:
ājagāma janasthānam rāghavaḥ pariśankitaḥ |
tam dīna mānasam dīnam āseduḥ mṛga pakṣiṇaḥ
verses.translation: Raghava came to Janasthaana doubting overly, and the animals and birds of Janasthaana which look doleful have neared him whose heart has become doleful.

glosses.meaning: at doleful Raghava, neared - the dole-hearted animals and birds neared that doleful Raghava.]

verses.devanagari:
सव्यम् कृत्वा महात्मानम् घोराम् च ससृजुः स्वरान् |
तानि दृष्ट्वा निमित्तानि महाघोराणि राघवः |
न्यवर्तत अथ त्वरितो जवेन आश्रमम् आत्मनः
verses.iast:
savyam kṛtvā mahātmānam ghorām ca sasṛjuḥ svarān |
tāni dṛṣṭvā nimittāni mahāghorāṇi rāghavaḥ |
nyavartata atha tvarito javena āśramam ātmanaḥ
verses.translation: Those doleful animals and birds moving in circumambulations from the left side to right of that noble-souled Rama they let off frightening shrieks, and then observing those highly forbidding foretokens Rama returned to his own hermitage hastily and hurriedly.
notes: It is ill-omened if the animals or birds move round from one's left to right side. anena mṛga pakṣiṇām apradakṣiṇa gamanam aśubhakaram iti uktyā pradakṣiṇa gamanam śubhakaram iti sūcitam - mṛgā vihangāḥ ca gatāḥ pradakṣiṇam mahībhṛtām kānkṣita kārya siddhaye | ratnamāla - dk

glosses.meaning: on to left, making - moving on to left
frightening, shrieks, they let off, also
to his own, to hermitage, returned.

verses.devanagari:
ततो लक्षणम् आयान्तम् ददर्श विगत प्रभम् |
ततो अविदूरे रामेण समीयाय स लक्ष्मणः
विषण्णः स विषण्णेन दुःखितो दुःख भागिना |
verses.iast:
tato lakṣaṇam āyāntam dadarśa vigata prabham |
tato avidūre rāmeṇa samīyāya sa lakṣmaṇaḥ
viṣaṇṇaḥ sa viṣaṇṇena duḥkhito duḥkha bhāginā |
verses.translation: Then Rama saw Lakshmana coming towards him with a lacklustre face, and then Lakshmana, who is melancholic and anguishing in his divergence from Seetha, met Rama not a long-way-off, where Rama is a similar partaker in melancholy and anguishing by way of his convergence upon ill-omens.

glosses.meaning: verily, gone [lacking,] lustre - with a lacklustre face

verses.devanagari:
संजगर्हे अथ तम् भ्राता दृष्टा लक्ष्मणम् आगतम्
विहाय सीताम् विजने वने राक्षस सेविते |
verses.iast:
sañjagarhe atha tam bhrātā dṛṣṭā lakṣmaṇam āgatam
vihāya sītām vijane vane rākṣasa sevite |
verses.translation: On seeing Lakshmana who has arrived at this place leaving off Seetha in a forest that is desolate, more so an adorable forest for demons, Rama reproached him as his elder brother.

glosses.meaning: Seetha, leaving off, who has come

verses.devanagari:
गृहीत्वा च करम् सव्यम् लक्ष्मणम् रघुनंदनः
उवाच मधुर उदर्कम् इदम् परुषम् आर्तवत् |
verses.iast:
gṛhītvā ca karam savyam lakṣmaṇam raghunaṃdanaḥ
uvāca madhura udarkam idam paruṣam ārtavat |
verses.translation: Taking Lakshmana's left hand into his, Rama, the descendent of Raghu, alike a bewailer spoke this brusque speech that has a mellowly fruition in future.
notes: This statement obtains two shades of meaning. One, the speech of Rama in reproaching Lakshmana though appear to be brusque, latently it is congratulatory to Lakshmana, to make happen the abduction of Seetha firstly, and thereby the ultimate elimination of Ravana. Two, he scolded Lakshmana prima facie for leaving Seetha, but on realising that he is not at fault, his speech is softened.

glosses.meaning: left, hand [of Lakshmana,] on taking [into his]
mellowly, futurity - words that have a maturity in future

verses.devanagari:
अहो लक्ष्मण गर्ह्यम् ते कृतम् यः त्वम् विहाय ताम्
सीताम् इह आगतः सौम्य कच्चित् स्वस्ति भवेत् इति |
verses.iast:
aho lakṣmaṇa garhyam te kṛtam yaḥ tvam vihāya tām
sītām iha āgataḥ saumya kaccit svasti bhavet iti |
verses.translation: "You have done a deplorable deed in coming here forsaking Seetha. Now, oh, gentle Lakshmana, are we somewhat safe, or everything has already gone astray now itself, or what.

verses.devanagari:
न मे अस्ति संशयो वीर सर्वथा जनकात्मजा
विनष्टा भक्षिता वा अप राक्षसैः वन चारिभिः |
अशुभानि एव भूयिष्ठम् यथा प्रादुर् भवन्ति मे
verses.iast:
na me asti saṃśayo vīra sarvathā janakātmajā
vinaṣṭā bhakṣitā vā apa rākṣasaiḥ vana cāribhiḥ |
aśubhāni eva bhūyiṣṭham yathā prādur bhavanti me
verses.translation: "Oh, brave one, according to these many inauspicious forebodings that have manifested themselves to me, we might have lost Janaka's daughter Seetha, or the forest ranging demons might have devoured her, or else they might have kidnapped her, I am doubtless about it.

glosses.meaning: to me, doubt, not, is there.

verses.devanagari:
अपि लक्ष्मण सीतायाः सामग्र्यम् प्राप्नुयावहे |
जीवन्त्याः पुरुषव्याघ्र सुताया जनक्स्य वै
verses.iast:
api lakṣmaṇa sītāyāḥ sāmagryam prāpnuyāvahe |
jīvantyāḥ puruṣavyāghra sutāyā janaksya vai
verses.translation: "Oh, tigerly-man Lakshmana, I wonder whether we can at least make out the daughter of Janaka Seetha in her intactness and aliveness.

glosses.meaning: at least, can we make out, really - I wonder.

verses.devanagari:
यथा वै मृग संघाःअ गोमायुः च भैरवम् |
वाश्यन्ते शकुनाः च अपि प्रदीप्ताम् अभितो दिशम् |
अपि स्वस्ति भवेत् तस्या राज पुत्र्या महाबल
verses.iast:
yathā vai mṛga saṃghāḥa gomāyuḥ ca bhairavam |
vāśyante śakunāḥ ca api pradīptām abhito diśam |
api svasti bhavet tasyā rāja putryā mahābala
verses.translation: "On observing these mobs of deer, this jackal, also even these birds which are voicing noisily facing the direction lit by the sun, oh, great-mighty Lakshmana, can we presume that there will be safety to that princes Seetha?

glosses.meaning: safety, even, will be there [or not,] really.

verses.devanagari:
इदम् हि रक्षो मृग संनिकाशम्
प्रलोभ्य माम् दूरम् अनुप्रयातम् |
हतम् कथंचित् महता श्रमेण
स राक्षसो अभूत् म्रियमाण एव
verses.iast:
idam hi rakṣo mṛga saṃnikāśam
pralobhya mām dūram anuprayātam |
hatam kathañcit mahatā śrameṇa
sa rākṣaso abhūt mriyamāṇa eva
verses.translation: "This very demon in his likeness to a deer led me on and led me off distantly as I was indeed following him, and by an intense effort somehow he was killed, and when dying he transfigured into a demon.

verses.devanagari:
मनः च मे दीनम् इह अप्रहृष्टम्
चक्षुः च सव्यम् कुरुते विकारम् |
असंशयम् लक्ष्मण न अस्ति सीता
हृता मृता वा पथि वर्तते वा
verses.iast:
manaḥ ca me dīnam iha aprahṛṣṭam
cakṣuḥ ca savyam kurute vikāram |
asaṃśayam lakṣmaṇa na asti sītā
hṛtā mṛtā vā pathi var.htate vā
verses.translation: "Now even my heart is woeful and I am woebegone, my left eye is also fluttering erratically, oh, Lakshmana, no doubt Seetha is not there in hermitage, maybe she is whisked away, or, wiped out, or, wandering around on a wrong way.
notes: The flutter of the left eye to males is ill-omened. anena puruShasya manaso asantoSho vaama netra sphuraNam ashubha suucakam iti uktyaa dakShiNa netra sphuraNam manaH santoShaH ca shubha kara iti suucitam | tathaa ca raghu vamshe kaalidaasaH - tasyaam raghoH suunu rupaa sthitaayaam vR^iNiita vaa neti samaakulo aabhuut | vaametaraH samshayam asya baahuH keyuura bandhhocHravasito nunoda || - dk - - - - - iti vaalmiiki raamaayaNe aadi kaavye araNya kaaNDe sapta pa.ncaashaH sargaH Thus, this is the 57th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.
